A4.3 Machine Learning Approaches HL

Topic A4: Machine Learning | Choosing the Right Tool

Retrieval Practice HL

Recall A4.2 (preprocessing) before algorithms.

  1. Why do we clean data before training a model?
  2. What is the difference between feature selection and dimensionality reduction?
  3. What is an outlier?

Press Down for answers

Answer 1

Why do we clean data before training a model?

To remove errors/duplicates/outliers so the model learns reliable patterns.

Answer 2

What is the difference between feature selection and dimensionality reduction?

Selection: keep some original features. Reduction: create fewer new features/components.

Answer 3

What is an outlier?

A data point far from typical values (can be an error or a rare valid case).

The Big Question HL

🤔 You have data. You want predictions.

Which ML approach should you choose?

❌ Common misconception: “There’s one best algorithm.”

Different tasks require different approaches.

✅ Reality: choose based on task, data, and how you will evaluate the model.

HL focus: explain/describe/outline — not writing lots of code.

HL A map of approaches

What kind of output do you need?
GoalApproachExample
Predict a numberRegressionhouse price
Predict a labelClassificationspam/not spam
Group similar itemsClusteringcustomer segments
Discover “items bought together”Association rulesbasket analysis

HL Linear regression (continuous prediction)

How can we predict a number based on a line of best fit?

Regression predicts a continuous value.

Linear regression models a straight-line relationship between features and output.

Example

Input: size, location → Output: house price

Output is a number, so it’s regression.

HL Classification (categorical prediction)

How do we choose one label from a set?

Classification predicts a category.

The model learns boundaries that separate classes.

Examples

Spam vs not spam

Fraud vs legitimate

🧠 Quick Check HL

A. Predict tomorrow’s temperature (°C)

B. Predict whether a photo is a cat or a dog

Identify which is regression and which is classification.

A: regression (continuous value)

B: classification (category)

HL Hyperparameter tuning

Why do two models trained on the same data perform differently?

Hyperparameters are settings chosen by the developer.

Tuning uses validation performance to choose good settings.

Poor tuning can lead to overfitting.

Examples

Number of clusters (k) in k-means

Tree depth in decision trees

Learning rate in neural networks

HL Clustering (unsupervised grouping)

How can we group items when we don’t have labels?

Clustering groups similar data points together.

Useful for segmentation (customers, behaviours, patterns).

Example

Group shoppers into “bargain hunters”, “premium buyers”, “occasional visitors”.

HL Association rule learning

How do supermarkets learn “people who buy X also buy Y”?

Association rules uncover relationships in large data sets.

Often used for recommendation and cross-selling.

Example rule

{pasta, tomatoes} → {parmesan}

🧠 Quick Check HL

A streaming company wants to discover “users who watched A and B often also watch C”.

Recommend clustering or association rules — and explain why.

Association rules — it’s about co-occurrence relationships (“A and B → C”), not grouping users into segments.

HL Reinforcement learning

How can an agent learn by trial and error?

An agent takes actions in an environment.

It receives a reward and updates its strategy to maximize long-term reward.

Used in robotics, game-playing, and some recommendation systems.

HL Genetic algorithms

How can “evolution” help find good solutions?

Start with a population of candidate solutions.

Evaluate fitness, then apply selection + crossover + mutation.

Repeat until solutions improve.

Used for

Optimization problems with huge search spaces (timetables, routing).

HL Artificial neural networks (ANNs)

How can a network of simple units model complex patterns?

ANNs have layers of neurons connected by weights.

An activation function adds non-linearity so the model can represent complex relationships.

Multi-layer networks can learn higher-level features from raw inputs.

Big picture

More layers can model more complex patterns — but increase risk of overfitting and computation cost.

HL Convolutional neural networks (CNNs)

Why are CNNs especially good for images?

CNNs use filters to detect local patterns (edges, textures).

Layers build a hierarchy: edges → shapes → objects.

Use cases

Image classification, object detection, medical imaging.

HL Model selection & comparison

How do we choose the “best” model without fooling ourselves?

Use a validation approach (train/validation/test or cross-validation).

Compare models using appropriate metrics (accuracy, error, etc.).

Watch for overfitting: strong training performance but weak test performance.

Misconception Check HL

True or False: “Higher training accuracy always means a better model.”

False. A model can overfit — memorizing training data rather than generalizing.

Use validation/testing (and cross-validation) to check performance on unseen data.

Key Takeaways HL

  • Use regression/classification for supervised prediction tasks.
  • Use clustering/association rules to discover structure in unlabelled data.
  • Reinforcement learning learns actions via rewards; genetic algorithms optimize via evolution.
  • ANNs and CNNs model complex patterns; tuning and evaluation prevent overfitting.
  • Model selection relies on fair comparison using validation and metrics.
